The Mondragon Corporation is a corporation and federation of worker cooperatives based in the Basque region of Spain.

It was founded in the town of Mondragón in 1956 by Father José María Arizmendiarrieta and a group of his students at a technical college he founded. Its first product was paraffin heaters.

It is the seventh-largest Spanish company in terms of asset turnover and the leading business group in the Basque Country. At the end of 2016, it employed 74,117 people in 257 companies and organizations in four areas of activity: finance, industry, retail and knowledge.[2] By 2019, 81,507 people were employed.[3] In 2024, it had over 70,000 workers, 30,660 in the Basque Country, 29,340 in the rest of Spain and around 10,000 abroad.[4] Mondragon cooperatives operate in accordance with the Statement on the Co-operative Identity maintained by the International Co-operative Alliance.

In 1941, as a young Catholic priest, José María Arizmendiarrieta settled in Mondragón, a town with a population of 7,000 that had not yet recovered from the poverty, hunger, exile, and tension of the Spanish Civil War.[5][6] In 1943, Arizmendiarrieta established a technical college which became a training ground for managers, engineers and skilled labour for local companies, and primarily for the co-operatives.[7]

Arizmendiarrieta spent a number of years educating young people about a form of humanism based on solidarity and participation, in harmony with Catholic social teaching, and the importance of acquiring the necessary technical knowledge before creating the first co-operative.

In 1955, he selected five young people to establish the first company of the co-operative and industrial beginning of the Mondragon Corporation. The company was called Talleres Ulgor ("Ulgor workshops"), an acronym derived from the surnames of Usatorre, Larrañaga, Gorroñogoitia, Ormaechea, and Ortubay, known today as Fagor Electrodomésticos (Spanish for "Fagor electric appliances").[8][page needed]

In the first 15 years, many co-operatives were established, thanks to the autarky of the market and the awakening of the Spanish economy. During these years, also with the encouragement of Arizmendiarrieta, the Caja Laboral ("Labor savings bank", 1959) and the Social Welfare Body Lagun Aro ("Friend/help time", 1966) were established that played a key role. The first local group was created, Ularco. In 1969, Eroski was founded by merging ten small local consumer co-operatives.[9][10]

During the next 20 years, from 1970 to 1990, the dynamic continued, with a strong increase in new co-operatives promoted by Caja Laboral's Business Division, the promotion of co-operative associations, the formation of local groups, and the founding of the Ikerlan ("Research work") research centre in 1974.[11]

With Spain scheduled to join the European Economic Community in 1986, it was decided in 1984 to establish the "Mondragon Co-operative Group", the forerunner of the current corporation. In-service training for managers was strengthened by creating Otalora, dedicated to training, and the dissemination of co-operatives. The Group consisted of 23,130 workers at the end of 1990.[12][non-primary source needed]

International expansion

[edit]

On the international stage, the aim was to respond to growing globalisation, expanding abroad by establishing production plants in a number of countries. The first was the Copreci plant in Mexico in 1990, followed by many others: up to 73 by the end of 2008, and 122 at the end of 2013. The goals were to increase competitiveness and market share, bring component supply closer to customers' plants, especially in the automotive and domestic appliance sectors, and to strengthen employment in the Basque Country by promoting exports of co-operatives' products by means of new platforms.[13]

Between 2002 and 2007, Fagor and Eroski issued bonds (aportaciones subordinadas). While they were commercialized as safe deposits, the courts classed them as riskier debt instruments. When the yields fell during the 2008 financial crisis, bond-holders sued against the cooperatives.[14]

In 2008, the worker-owners of the cooperatives Ampo (metal casting) and Irizar (coaches) voted to leave the corporation.[14]

In October 2009, the United Steelworkers announced an agreement with Mondragon to create worker cooperatives in the United States.[15] On 26 March 2012, the USW, Mondragon, and the Ohio Employee Ownership Center (OEOC) announced their detailed union co-op model.[16]

The industrial sector ended 2012 with a new record of €4 billion in international sales, beating sales figures from before the 2008 financial crisis. Mondragon opened 11 new production subsidiaries. International sales that year accounted for 69% of all sales, a 26% increase from 2009 to 2012, and with 14,000 employees abroad. Mondragon's share in the BRIC markets increased to 20% compared to the previous year.[17] In 2013, international sales grew by 6.7% and accounted for 71.1% of total sales.[18]

On 16 October 2013, domestic appliance company Fagor Electrodomésticos filed for bankruptcy under Spanish law to renegotiate €1.1 billion of debt, after suffering heavy losses during the euro area crisis and the 2008–2014 Spanish real estate crisis, putting 5,600 employees at risk of losing their jobs.[19] This was followed by the bankruptcy of the whole Fagor group on 6 November 2013.[20] In July 2014, Fagor was bought by Catalonian company Cata for €42.5 million. Cata pledged to create 705 direct jobs in the Basque Country and to continue the brand names Fagor, Edesa, Aspes, and Splendid.[21]

In 2022, the worker-owners of ULMA Group (scaffolding) and Orona (elevators) voted to leave the corporation. Estimated impact of the leave is a workforce drop by 13% and a 15% cut of the group's sales.[22] As successful cooperatives they were contributing 10% of their profit to a common fund supporting ailing cooperatives. They will not contribute to the solidarity fund but they will keep insuring their workers with Lagun Aro and collaborate with Mondragon Unibertsitatea and other cooperatives in the group.[14]

Mondragon co-operatives are united by a humanist concept of business, a philosophy of participation and solidarity, and a shared business culture. The culture is rooted in a shared mission and a number of principles, corporate values and business policies.[23]

Over the years, these links have been embodied in a series of operating rules approved on a majority basis by the Co-operative Congresses, which regulate the activity of the Governing Bodies of the corporation (Standing Committee, General Council), the Grassroots Co-operatives and the Divisions they belong to, from the organisational, institutional and economic points of view as well as in terms of assets.[24][non-primary source needed]

This framework of business culture has been structured based on a common culture derived from the 10 Basic Co-operative Principles, in which Mondragon is rooted: Open Admission, Democratic Organisation, the Sovereignty of Labour, Instrumental and Subordinate Nature of Capital, Participatory Management, Payment Solidarity, Inter-cooperation, Social Transformation, Universality and Education.[25][non-primary source needed]

This philosophy is complemented by four corporate values: Co-operation, acting as owners and protagonists; Participation, which takes shape as a commitment to management; Social Responsibility, by means of the distribution of wealth based on solidarity; and Innovation, focusing on constant renewal in all areas.[26]

This business culture translates into compliance with a number of Basic Objectives (Customer Focus, Development, Innovation, Profitability, People in Co-operation and Involvement in the Community) and General Policies approved by the Co-operative Congress, which are taken on board at all the corporation's organisational levels and incorporated into the four-year strategic plans and the annual business plans of the individual co-operatives, divisions, and the corporation as a whole.[27][non-primary source needed]

At Mondragon, there are agreed-upon wage ratios between executive work and field or factory work which earns a minimum wage. These ratios range from 3:1 to 9:1 in different cooperatives and average 5:1. That is, the general manager of an average Mondragon cooperative earns no more than 5 times as much as the theoretical minimum wage paid in their cooperative. For most workers, this ratio is smaller because there are few Mondragon worker-owners that earn minimum wages, because most jobs are somewhat specialized and are classified at higher wage levels. The wage ratio of a cooperative is decided periodically by its worker-owners through a democratic vote.[28]

Compared to similar jobs at local industries, Mondragon managers' wages were 30% lower in 1991 (as some companies pay their best paid managers hundreds of times more than the lowest-paid employee of the company)[29] and equivalent for middle management, technical and professional levels. Lower wage levels are on average 13% higher than similar jobs at local businesses. Spain's progressive tax rate further reduces any disparity in pay.[28] These comparatively low wages can make it very difficult to recruit managers from investor-owned firms.[30]

Mondragon Corporation operates in four areas: finance, industry, retail, and knowledge, with the latter distinguishing Mondragon from other business groups. In 2013, the corporation posted a total revenue of over €12 billion (roughly US$16 billion), and employed 74,061 workers,[2] making it Spain's fourth-largest industrial and tenth-largest financial group.[31]

This area includes the banking business of Laboral Kutxa (successor of Caja Laboral), the insurance company Seguros Lagun Aro, and the Voluntary Social Welfare Body Lagun Aro, which had an asset fund totaling €5,566 million at the end of 2014. The yield obtained from this fund is used to cover long-term retirement, widowhood, and invalidity benefits, complementary to those offered by the Spanish social security system.

The corporation's companies manufacture consumer goods, capital goods, industrial components, products, and systems for construction, and services. The latter includes very diverse business groups such as:

  • Abantail: Adaptive design optimization
  • Alecop: Engineering training
  • LKS Consultores: Legal services
  • KREAN: Architects and engineers.
  • MCCTelecom: Telecommunication engineering.
  • Mondragon Lingua: Translation and language schools
  • Mondragon Sistemas: Automation, Industrial Computing and Telecommunications.
  • Ondoan: Turnkey projects in the energy and environmental sector. In the leisure and sports area, it manufactures Orbea bicycles, exercise equipment and items for camping, garden and beach.[32]

[33]

In capital goods, Mondragon posted a turnover of €976 million in 2009 and is the leading Spanish manufacturer of machining (Danobat Group) and sheet metal forming (Fagor Arrasate Group) machine tools. These machines are complemented by automation and control products for machine tools, packaging machinery, machinery for automating assembly processes and processing wood, forklift trucks, electric transformers, integrated equipment for the catering industry, cold stores, and refrigeration equipment. Specifically focusing on the automotive sector, the corporation also manufactures a wide variety of dies, molds and tooling for casting iron and aluminium, and occupies a leading position in machinery for the casting sector.[34]

In Industrial Components, Mondragon posted a turnover of €1.5 billion in 2009, a sector in which it operates as an integrated supplier for the leading car manufacturers, offering from the design and development of a part to the industrialization and supply of components and assemblies. It has different business units such as brakes, axles, suspension, transmission, engines, aluminium wheel rims, fluid conduction, and other internal and external vehicle components. It also produces components for the main domestic appliance manufacturers in three business areas: white goods, home comfort, and electronics. And it manufactures flanges and pipe accessories for processing oil-gas, petrochemical plants and power generation, copper and aluminium electrical conductors, and components for conveyors.[35]

In construction, sales totaled €974 million in 2009. Mondragon has constructed buildings and important infrastructure projects. It designs and builds large metallic (URSSA), laminated wood and prefabricated concrete structures; supplies prefabricated parts in polymer concrete; offers solutions[buzzword] for formwork and structures (ULMA Group) as well as public works machinery and the industrialization of the construction process, including engineering and assembly services. The ORONA Group produces elevators.[36]

In services to business, sales totaled €248 million in 2008, including business consultancy services, architecture and engineering, property consulting, design and innovation (LKS Group), systems engineering for electromechanical installations, and integrated logistics engineering. It also offers a modern language service, manufactures educational equipment, and provides graphic arts services (mccgraphics S.Coop).[citation needed]

In 2013, 71.1% of turnover came from international sales. Sales resulting from the export of products abroad and production generated in the 122 subsidiaries located in several different countries: China (15), France (17), Poland (8), Czech Republic (7), Mexico (8), Brazil (5), Germany (4), Italy (4), United Kingdom (3), Romania (3), United States (4), Turkey (2), Portugal (2), Slovakia (2), India (5), Thailand (1) and Morocco (1). Overall, in 2013 these 122 plants provided work for more than 11,000 people. The corporate industrial park in Kunshan, close to Shanghai houses seven subsidiaries.[37] In 2012, it opened 11 new subsidiaries abroad, employing around 14,000 people. Its international sales that year marked a record number of 69% of its total sales (€5.8 billion, with a 2% fall compared to the previous year). Mondragon also participated in 91 international R&D projects.[38]

In 2014, the industrial cooperatives created 1,000 jobs, and internationalization continued with 125 production subsidiaries abroad – 3 more than the year before.[39]

Mondragon runs Eroski, one of the leading retail groups throughout Spain and southern France, and maintains close contacts with the French group Les Mousquetaires and the German retailer Edeka, with whom it set up the Alidis international purchasing group in 2002. The worker-owners and consumer-members participate in the co-operative's decision-making bodies and management of Eroski.[40] At the end of 2013, Eroski posted a turnover of €6.6 billion, operating 2.069 stores made up of 90 Eroski hypermarkets, 1,211 Eroski/center, Caprabo, Eroski/city, Aliprox, Familia, Onda and Cash & Carry supermarkets, 155 branches of Eroski travel agencies, 63 petrol stations, 39 Forum Sport stores and 221 IF perfume stores.[41] In southern France Eroski had 4 hypermarkets, 16 supermarkets and 17 petrol stations, and 4 perfume stores in Andorra.[42]

Retail includes the food group Erkop, for catering, cleaning, stock-breeding, and horticulture with Auzo Lagun, a co-operative in group catering and cleaning of buildings and premises, and integrated service in the health sector.[43] In 2008, worker-members voted to expand the cooperative transformation to the retail group as a whole, turning subsidiaries into co-operatives, and making salaried workers worker-members.[44]

This area has a dual focus: education-training and innovation, which have both been key elements in the development of the corporation. Training-education is mainly linked to the dynamism of Mondragon University, the significant role that Politeknika Ikastegia Txorierri, Arizmendi Ikastola and Lea Artibai Ikastetxea play in their respective areas and the activity of the Management and Co-operative Development Centre Otalora.[45][46]

Mondragon University is a co-operative university, which combines the development of knowledge, skills, and values, and maintains close relations with business, especially Mondragon co-operatives. Technological innovation is generated through the co-operatives' own R&D departments, the Corporate Science and Technology Plan, the corporation's 12 technology centers and the Garaia Innovation Park.[47]

The 15 technology centers play a fundamental role in the development of the sectors of focus. In 2009 they employed 742 people and had a budget of €53.7 million.[48] In 2013 its network of technology centers and R&D units provided employment for 1,700 people and the commitment to R&D&I matters amounted to 136 million Euros, 8.5% of added value.[18] Mondragon has 479 families of Patents for Inventions, which accounts for 25% patents in the Basque Country, participating in more than 30 R&D cooperation projects at the European level.[39]

In 2012, Richard D. Wolff, an American professor of economics, hailed the Mondragon set of enterprises, including the good wages it provides for employees, the empowerment of ordinary workers in decision making, and the measure of equality for female workers, as a major success and cited it as a working model of an alternative to the capitalist mode of production.[49]

In an April 2012 interview, Noam Chomsky said that, while Mondragon offers an alternative to capitalism, it was still embedded in a capitalist system which limits Mondragon's decisions:[50]

Take the most advanced case: Mondragon. It's worker-owned, it's not worker managed, although the management does come from the workforce often, but it's in a market system and they still exploit workers in South America, and they do things that are harmful to the society as a whole and they have no choice. If you're in a system where you must make a profit in order to survive, you're compelled to ignore negative externalities, effects on others.

Vicenç Navarro wrote that, from a business perspective, Mondragon is successful in matching efficiency with solidarity and democracy. However, he writes that the number of employees who are not owners has increased more rapidly than worker-owners, to a point that in some companies, for example in the supermarket chains owned by Mondragon, the first is a much larger group than the second. In Navarro's view, this establishes a two-tier system – for example, in terms of whom to save in the case the company collapses. In the collapse of Fagor, the relocation of employees to other companies belonging to Mondragon favored those who were worker-owners, which may affect labor relations:[51]

Actually, one of the successes of Mondragon was its ability to create a sense of identity among the workers within the company, encouraging an environment of solidarity and collegiality among them, a feeling that also extended (although to a much lesser degree) to non-worker-owners. The connection felt by the latter group has somewhat weakened, however, exposing a vulnerable point for the cooperative.

The Mondragon system is one of four case studies analyzed in Capital and the Debt Trap, which summarized evidence claiming that cooperatives tend to last longer and are less susceptible to perverse incentives and other problems of organizational governance than more traditionally managed organizations.

The founders of Cooperation Jackson, a network of worker cooperatives in Jackson, Mississippi in the United States, cite Mondragon as a key inspiration.[52]

Kim Stanley Robinson's science fiction novels depict a future where the Mondragon Corporation is prominent. The Mondragon Corporation appeared in Robinson's works Mars trilogy,[53][54] The Ministry for the Future,[55] in the novel 2312 which features a world where the Mondragon Corporation has evolved into a planned economy system called the Mondragon Accord.[56].

(December 2022) Mondragon CorporationTypeWorker cooperative federationFounded14 April 1956FounderJosé María ArizmendiarrietaHeadquarters Mondragón, Basque Country, SpainArea servedInternationalKey peoplePello Rodríguez (president of the General Council)[1]Revenue€11.213 billion (2024)[1]Number of employees70,085 (2024)[1]DivisionsFinance, Industry, Retail, Knowledge[1]Websitemondragon-corporation.com The Mondragon Corporation is a corporation and federation of worker cooperatives based in the Basque region of Spain. It was founded in the town of Mondragón in 1956 by Father José María Arizmendiarrieta and a group of his students at a technical college he founded. Its first product was paraffin heaters. It is the seventh-largest Spanish company in terms of asset turnover and the leading business group in the Basque Country. At the end of 2016, it employed 74,117 people in 257 companies and organizations in four areas of activity: finance, industry, retail and knowledge.[2] By 2019, 81,507 people were employed.[3] In 2024, it had over 70,000 workers, 30,660 in the Basque Country, 29,340 in the rest of Spain and around 10,000 abroad.[4] Mondragon cooperatives operate in accordance with the Statement on the Co-operative Identity maintained by the International Co-operative Alliance. In 1941, as a young Catholic priest, José María Arizmendiarrieta settled in Mondragón, a town with a population of 7,000 that had not yet recovered from the poverty, hunger, exile, and tension of the Spanish Civil War.[5][6] In 1943, Arizmendiarrieta established a technical college which became a training ground for managers, engineers and skilled labour for local companies, and primarily for the co-operatives.[7] Arizmendiarrieta spent a number of years educating young people about a form of humanism based on solidarity and participation, in harmony with Catholic social teaching, and the importance of acquiring the necessary technical knowledge before creating the first co-operative. In 1955, he selected five young people to establish the first company of the co-operative and industrial beginning of the Mondragon Corporation. The company was called Talleres Ulgor ("Ulgor workshops"), an acronym derived from the surnames of Usatorre, Larrañaga, Gorroñogoitia, Ormaechea, and Ortubay, known today as Fagor Electrodomésticos (Spanish for "Fagor electric appliances").[8][page needed] In the first 15 years, many co-operatives were established, thanks to the autarky of the market and the awakening of the Spanish economy. During these years, also with the encouragement of Arizmendiarrieta, the Caja Laboral ("Labor savings bank", 1959) and the Social Welfare Body Lagun Aro ("Friend/help time", 1966) were established that played a key role. The first local group was created, Ularco. In 1969, Eroski was founded by merging ten small local consumer co-operatives.[9][10] During the next 20 years, from 1970 to 1990, the dynamic continued, with a strong increase in new co-operatives promoted by Caja Laboral's Business Division, the promotion of co-operative associations, the formation of local groups, and the founding of the Ikerlan ("Research work") research centre in 1974.[11] With Spain scheduled to join the European Economic Community in 1986, it was decided in 1984 to establish the "Mondragon Co-operative Group", the forerunner of the current corporation. In-service training for managers was strengthened by creating Otalora, dedicated to training, and the dissemination of co-operatives. The Group consisted of 23,130 workers at the end of 1990.[12][non-primary source needed] International expansion[edit] On the international stage, the aim was to respond to growing globalisation, expanding abroad by establishing production plants in a number of countries. The first was the Copreci plant in Mexico in 1990, followed by many others: up to 73 by the end of 2008, and 122 at the end of 2013. The goals were to increase competitiveness and market share, bring component supply closer to customers' plants, especially in the automotive and domestic appliance sectors, and to strengthen employment in the Basque Country by promoting exports of co-operatives' products by means of new platforms.[13] Between 2002 and 2007, Fagor and Eroski issued bonds (aportaciones subordinadas). While they were commercialized as safe deposits, the courts classed them as riskier debt instruments. When the yields fell during the 2008 financial crisis, bond-holders sued against the cooperatives.[14] In 2008, the worker-owners of the cooperatives Ampo (metal casting) and Irizar (coaches) voted to leave the corporation.[14] In October 2009, the United Steelworkers announced an agreement with Mondragon to create worker cooperatives in the United States.[15] On 26 March 2012, the USW, Mondragon, and the Ohio Employee Ownership Center (OEOC) announced their detailed union co-op model.[16] The industrial sector ended 2012 with a new record of €4 billion in international sales, beating sales figures from before the 2008 financial crisis. Mondragon opened 11 new production subsidiaries. International sales that year accounted for 69% of all sales, a 26% increase from 2009 to 2012, and with 14,000 employees abroad. Mondragon's share in the BRIC markets increased to 20% compared to the previous year.[17] In 2013, international sales grew by 6.7% and accounted for 71.1% of total sales.[18] On 16 October 2013, domestic appliance company Fagor Electrodomésticos filed for bankruptcy under Spanish law to renegotiate €1.1 billion of debt, after suffering heavy losses during the euro area crisis and the 2008–2014 Spanish real estate crisis, putting 5,600 employees at risk of losing their jobs.[19] This was followed by the bankruptcy of the whole Fagor group on 6 November 2013.[20] In July 2014, Fagor was bought by Catalonian company Cata for €42.5 million. Cata pledged to create 705 direct jobs in the Basque Country and to continue the brand names Fagor, Edesa, Aspes, and Splendid.[21] In 2022, the worker-owners of ULMA Group (scaffolding) and Orona (elevators) voted to leave the corporation. Estimated impact of the leave is a workforce drop by 13% and a 15% cut of the group's sales.[22] As successful cooperatives they were contributing 10% of their profit to a common fund supporting ailing cooperatives. They will not contribute to the solidarity fund but they will keep insuring their workers with Lagun Aro and collaborate with Mondragon Unibertsitatea and other cooperatives in the group.[14] Mondragon co-operatives are united by a humanist concept of business, a philosophy of participation and solidarity, and a shared business culture. The culture is rooted in a shared mission and a number of principles, corporate values and business policies.[23] Over the years, these links have been embodied in a series of operating rules approved on a majority basis by the Co-operative Congresses, which regulate the activity of the Governing Bodies of the corporation (Standing Committee, General Council), the Grassroots Co-operatives and the Divisions they belong to, from the organisational, institutional and economic points of view as well as in terms of assets.[24][non-primary source needed] Iñigo Ucín, president of Mondragon Corporation since 2016 This framework of business culture has been structured based on a common culture derived from the 10 Basic Co-operative Principles, in which Mondragon is rooted: Open Admission, Democratic Organisation, the Sovereignty of Labour, Instrumental and Subordinate Nature of Capital, Participatory Management, Payment Solidarity, Inter-cooperation, Social Transformation, Universality and Education.[25][non-primary source needed] This philosophy is complemented by four corporate values: Co-operation, acting as owners and protagonists; Participation, which takes shape as a commitment to management; Social Responsibility, by means of the distribution of wealth based on solidarity; and Innovation, focusing on constant renewal in all areas.[26] This business culture translates into compliance with a number of Basic Objectives (Customer Focus, Development, Innovation, Profitability, People in Co-operation and Involvement in the Community) and General Policies approved by the Co-operative Congress, which are taken on board at all the corporation's organisational levels and incorporated into the four-year strategic plans and the annual business plans of the individual co-operatives, divisions, and the corporation as a whole.[27][non-primary source needed] At Mondragon, there are agreed-upon wage ratios between executive work and field or factory work which earns a minimum wage. These ratios range from 3:1 to 9:1 in different cooperatives and average 5:1. That is, the general manager of an average Mondragon cooperative earns no more than 5 times as much as the theoretical minimum wage paid in their cooperative. For most workers, this ratio is smaller because there are few Mondragon worker-owners that earn minimum wages, because most jobs are somewhat specialized and are classified at higher wage levels. The wage ratio of a cooperative is decided periodically by its worker-owners through a democratic vote.[28] Compared to similar jobs at local industries, Mondragon managers' wages were 30% lower in 1991 (as some companies pay their best paid managers hundreds of times more than the lowest-paid employee of the company)[29] and equivalent for middle management, technical and professional levels. Lower wage levels are on average 13% higher than similar jobs at local businesses. Spain's progressive tax rate further reduces any disparity in pay.[28] These comparatively low wages can make it very difficult to recruit managers from investor-owned firms.[30] Mondragon Corporation operates in four areas: finance, industry, retail, and knowledge, with the latter distinguishing Mondragon from other business groups. In 2013, the corporation posted a total revenue of over €12 billion (roughly US$16 billion), and employed 74,061 workers,[2] making it Spain's fourth-largest industrial and tenth-largest financial group.[31] This area includes the banking business of Laboral Kutxa (successor of Caja Laboral), the insurance company Seguros Lagun Aro, and the Voluntary Social Welfare Body Lagun Aro, which had an asset fund totaling €5,566 million at the end of 2014. The yield obtained from this fund is used to cover long-term retirement, widowhood, and invalidity benefits, complementary to those offered by the Spanish social security system. The corporation's companies manufacture consumer goods, capital goods, industrial components, products, and systems for construction, and services. The latter includes very diverse business groups such as: Abantail: Adaptive design optimization Alecop: Engineering training LKS Consultores: Legal services KREAN: Architects and engineers. MCCTelecom: Telecommunication engineering. Mondragon Lingua: Translation and language schools Mondragon Sistemas: Automation, Industrial Computing and Telecommunications. Ondoan: Turnkey projects in the energy and environmental sector. In the leisure and sports area, it manufactures Orbea bicycles, exercise equipment and items for camping, garden and beach.[32] [33] In capital goods, Mondragon posted a turnover of €976 million in 2009 and is the leading Spanish manufacturer of machining (Danobat Group) and sheet metal forming (Fagor Arrasate Group) machine tools. These machines are complemented by automation and control products for machine tools, packaging machinery, machinery for automating assembly processes and processing wood, forklift trucks, electric transformers, integrated equipment for the catering industry, cold stores, and refrigeration equipment. Specifically focusing on the automotive sector, the corporation also manufactures a wide variety of dies, molds and tooling for casting iron and aluminium, and occupies a leading position in machinery for the casting sector.[34] In Industrial Components, Mondragon posted a turnover of €1.5 billion in 2009, a sector in which it operates as an integrated supplier for the leading car manufacturers, offering from the design and development of a part to the industrialization and supply of components and assemblies. It has different business units such as brakes, axles, suspension, transmission, engines, aluminium wheel rims, fluid conduction, and other internal and external vehicle components. It also produces components for the main domestic appliance manufacturers in three business areas: white goods, home comfort, and electronics. And it manufactures flanges and pipe accessories for processing oil-gas, petrochemical plants and power generation, copper and aluminium electrical conductors, and components for conveyors.[35] In construction, sales totaled €974 million in 2009. Mondragon has constructed buildings and important infrastructure projects. It designs and builds large metallic (URSSA), laminated wood and prefabricated concrete structures; supplies prefabricated parts in polymer concrete; offers solutions[buzzword] for formwork and structures (ULMA Group) as well as public works machinery and the industrialization of the construction process, including engineering and assembly services. The ORONA Group produces elevators.[36] In services to business, sales totaled €248 million in 2008, including business consultancy services, architecture and engineering, property consulting, design and innovation (LKS Group), systems engineering for electromechanical installations, and integrated logistics engineering. It also offers a modern language service, manufactures educational equipment, and provides graphic arts services (mccgraphics S.Coop).[citation needed] In 2013, 71.1% of turnover came from international sales. Sales resulting from the export of products abroad and production generated in the 122 subsidiaries located in several different countries: China (15), France (17), Poland (8), Czech Republic (7), Mexico (8), Brazil (5), Germany (4), Italy (4), United Kingdom (3), Romania (3), United States (4), Turkey (2), Portugal (2), Slovakia (2), India (5), Thailand (1) and Morocco (1). Overall, in 2013 these 122 plants provided work for more than 11,000 people. The corporate industrial park in Kunshan, close to Shanghai houses seven subsidiaries.[37] In 2012, it opened 11 new subsidiaries abroad, employing around 14,000 people. Its international sales that year marked a record number of 69% of its total sales (€5.8 billion, with a 2% fall compared to the previous year). Mondragon also participated in 91 international R&D projects.[38] In 2014, the industrial cooperatives created 1,000 jobs, and internationalization continued with 125 production subsidiaries abroad – 3 more than the year before.[39] Mondragon runs Eroski, one of the leading retail groups throughout Spain and southern France, and maintains close contacts with the French group Les Mousquetaires and the German retailer Edeka, with whom it set up the Alidis international purchasing group in 2002. The worker-owners and consumer-members participate in the co-operative's decision-making bodies and management of Eroski.[40] At the end of 2013, Eroski posted a turnover of €6.6 billion, operating 2.069 stores made up of 90 Eroski hypermarkets, 1,211 Eroski/center, Caprabo, Eroski/city, Aliprox, Familia, Onda and Cash & Carry supermarkets, 155 branches of Eroski travel agencies, 63 petrol stations, 39 Forum Sport stores and 221 IF perfume stores.[41] In southern France Eroski had 4 hypermarkets, 16 supermarkets and 17 petrol stations, and 4 perfume stores in Andorra.[42] Retail includes the food group Erkop, for catering, cleaning, stock-breeding, and horticulture with Auzo Lagun, a co-operative in group catering and cleaning of buildings and premises, and integrated service in the health sector.[43] In 2008, worker-members voted to expand the cooperative transformation to the retail group as a whole, turning subsidiaries into co-operatives, and making salaried workers worker-members.[44] This area has a dual focus: education-training and innovation, which have both been key elements in the development of the corporation. Training-education is mainly linked to the dynamism of Mondragon University, the significant role that Politeknika Ikastegia Txorierri, Arizmendi Ikastola and Lea Artibai Ikastetxea play in their respective areas and the activity of the Management and Co-operative Development Centre Otalora.[45][46] Mondragon University is a co-operative university, which combines the development of knowledge, skills, and values, and maintains close relations with business, especially Mondragon co-operatives. Technological innovation is generated through the co-operatives' own R&D departments, the Corporate Science and Technology Plan, the corporation's 12 technology centers and the Garaia Innovation Park.[47] The 15 technology centers play a fundamental role in the development of the sectors of focus. In 2009 they employed 742 people and had a budget of €53.7 million.[48] In 2013 its network of technology centers and R&D units provided employment for 1,700 people and the commitment to R&D&I matters amounted to 136 million Euros, 8.5% of added value.[18] Mondragon has 479 families of Patents for Inventions, which accounts for 25% patents in the Basque Country, participating in more than 30 R&D cooperation projects at the European level.[39] In 2012, Richard D. Wolff, an American professor of economics, hailed the Mondragon set of enterprises, including the good wages it provides for employees, the empowerment of ordinary workers in decision making, and the measure of equality for female workers, as a major success and cited it as a working model of an alternative to the capitalist mode of production.[49] In an April 2012 interview, Noam Chomsky said that, while Mondragon offers an alternative to capitalism, it was still embedded in a capitalist system which limits Mondragon's decisions:[50] Take the most advanced case: Mondragon. It's worker-owned, it's not worker managed, although the management does come from the workforce often, but it's in a market system and they still exploit workers in South America, and they do things that are harmful to the society as a whole and they have no choice. If you're in a system where you must make a profit in order to survive, you're compelled to ignore negative externalities, effects on others. Vicenç Navarro wrote that, from a business perspective, Mondragon is successful in matching efficiency with solidarity and democracy. However, he writes that the number of employees who are not owners has increased more rapidly than worker-owners, to a point that in some companies, for example in the supermarket chains owned by Mondragon, the first is a much larger group than the second. In Navarro's view, this establishes a two-tier system – for example, in terms of whom to save in the case the company collapses. In the collapse of Fagor, the relocation of employees to other companies belonging to Mondragon favored those who were worker-owners, which may affect labor relations:[51] Actually, one of the successes of Mondragon was its ability to create a sense of identity among the workers within the company, encouraging an environment of solidarity and collegiality among them, a feeling that also extended (although to a much lesser degree) to non-worker-owners. The connection felt by the latter group has somewhat weakened, however, exposing a vulnerable point for the cooperative. The Mondragon system is one of four case studies analyzed in Capital and the Debt Trap, which summarized evidence claiming that cooperatives tend to last longer and are less susceptible to perverse incentives and other problems of organizational governance than more traditionally managed organizations. The founders of Cooperation Jackson, a network of worker cooperatives in Jackson, Mississippi in the United States, cite Mondragon as a key inspiration.[52] Kim Stanley Robinson's science fiction novels depict a future where the Mondragon Corporation is prominent. The Mondragon Corporation appeared in Robinson's works Mars trilogy,[53][54] The Ministry for the Future,[55] in the novel 2312 which features a world where the Mondragon Corporation has evolved into a planned economy system called the Mondragon Accord.[56]. blocks.html_en: The Mondragon Corporation is a corporation and federation of worker cooperatives based in the Basque region of Spain.

sentences.en: The Mondragon Corporation is a corporation and federation of worker cooperatives based in the Basque region of Spain.
sentences.zh: 蒙德拉贡公司是一家位于西班牙巴斯克地区的公司和工人合作社联合会。

blocks.html_en: It was founded in the town of Mondragón in 1956 by Father José María Arizmendiarrieta and a group of his students at a technical college he founded. Its first product was paraffin heaters.

sentences.en: It was founded in the town of Mondragón in 1956 by Father José María Arizmendiarrieta and a group of his students at a technical college he founded.
sentences.zh: 它于 1956 年由 José María Arizmendiarrieta 神父和他创办的一所技术学院的一群学生在蒙德拉贡镇创立。

sentences.en: Its first product was paraffin heaters.
sentences.zh: 它的第一个产品是石蜡加热器。

blocks.html_en: It is the seventh-largest Spanish company in terms of asset turnover and the leading business group in the Basque Country. At the end of 2016, it employed 74,117 people in 257 companies and organizations in four areas of activity: finance, industry, retail and knowledge.[2] By 2019, 81,507 people were employed.[3] In 2024, it had over 70,000 workers, 30,660 in the Basque Country, 29,340 in the rest of Spain and around 10,000 abroad.[4] Mondragon cooperatives operate in accordance with the Statement on the Co-operative Identity maintained by the International Co-operative Alliance.

sentences.en: It is the seventh-largest Spanish company in terms of asset turnover and the leading business group in the Basque Country.
sentences.zh: 按资产周转率计算，它是西班牙第七大公司，也是巴斯克地区领先的商业集团。

sentences.en: At the end of 2016, it employed 74,117 people in 257 companies and organizations in four areas of activity: finance, industry, retail and knowledge.[2] By 2019, 81,507 people were employed.[3] In 2024, it had over 70,000 workers, 30,660 in the Basque Country, 29,340 in the rest of Spain and around 10,000 abroad.[4] Mondragon cooperatives operate in accordance with the Statement on the Co-operative Identity maintained by the International Co-operative Alliance.
sentences.zh: 截至 2016 年底，该公司在 257 家公司和组织中雇用了 74,117 名员工，涉及四个活动领域：金融、工业、零售和知识。 [2]截至2019年，就业人数81,507人。[3] 2024 年，该公司拥有超过 70,000 名工人，其中 30,660 人在巴斯克地区，29,340 人在西班牙其他地区，约 10,000 人在国外。[4]蒙德拉贡合作社按照国际合作社联盟维护的合作社身份声明进行运营。

blocks.html_en: In 1941, as a young Catholic priest, José María Arizmendiarrieta settled in Mondragón, a town with a population of 7,000 that had not yet recovered from the poverty, hunger, exile, and tension of the Spanish Civil War.[5][6] In 1943, Arizmendiarrieta established a technical college which became a training ground for managers, engineers and skilled labour for local companies, and primarily for the co-operatives.[7]

sentences.en: In 1941, as a young Catholic priest, José María Arizmendiarrieta settled in Mondragón, a town with a population of 7,000 that had not yet recovered from the poverty, hunger, exile, and tension of the Spanish Civil War.[5][6] In 1943, Arizmendiarrieta established a technical college which became a training ground for managers, engineers and skilled labour for local companies, and primarily for the co-operatives.[7]
sentences.zh: 1941年，作为一名年轻的天主教神父，何塞·玛丽亚·阿里兹曼迪亚里亚塔 (José María Arizmendiarrieta) 定居在蒙德拉贡 (Mondragón)，这座人口只有 7,000 人的小镇尚未从西班牙内战的贫困、饥饿、流放和紧张局势中恢复过来。[5][6] 1943 年，Arizmendiarrieta 建立了一所技术学院，成为当地公司（主要是合作社）经理、工程师和熟练工人的培训基地。 [7]

blocks.html_en: Arizmendiarrieta spent a number of years educating young people about a form of humanism based on solidarity and participation, in harmony with Catholic social teaching, and the importance of acquiring the necessary technical knowledge before creating the first co-operative.

sentences.en: Arizmendiarrieta spent a number of years educating young people about a form of humanism based on solidarity and participation, in harmony with Catholic social teaching, and the importance of acquiring the necessary technical knowledge before creating the first co-operative.
sentences.zh: Arizmendiarrieta 花了数年时间教育年轻人一种基于团结和参与的人文主义形式，与天主教社会教义相协调，以及在创建第一个合作社之前获得必要的技术知识的重要性。

blocks.html_en: In 1955, he selected five young people to establish the first company of the co-operative and industrial beginning of the Mondragon Corporation. The company was called Talleres Ulgor ("Ulgor workshops"), an acronym derived from the surnames of Usatorre, Larrañaga, Gorroñogoitia, Ormaechea, and Ortubay, known today as Fagor Electrodomésticos (Spanish for "Fagor electric appliances").[8][page needed]

sentences.en: In 1955, he selected five young people to establish the first company of the co-operative and industrial beginning of the Mondragon Corporation.
sentences.zh: 1955年，他挑选了五位年轻人成立了蒙德拉贡公司第一家合作社和工业公司。

sentences.en: The company was called Talleres Ulgor ("Ulgor workshops"), an acronym derived from the surnames of Usatorre, Larrañaga, Gorroñogoitia, Ormaechea, and Ortubay, known today as Fagor Electrodomésticos (Spanish for "Fagor electric appliances").[8][page needed]
sentences.zh: 该公司名为 Talleres Ulgor（“Ulgor 作坊”），是源自 Usatorre、Larrañaga、Gorroñogoitia、Ormaechea 和 Ortubay 等姓氏的缩写，今天称为 Fagor Electrodomésticos（西班牙语，意为“法格电器”）。[8][需要页面]

blocks.html_en: In the first 15 years, many co-operatives were established, thanks to the autarky of the market and the awakening of the Spanish economy. During these years, also with the encouragement of Arizmendiarrieta, the Caja Laboral ("Labor savings bank", 1959) and the Social Welfare Body Lagun Aro ("Friend/help time", 1966) were established that played a key role. The first local group was created, Ularco. In 1969, Eroski was founded by merging ten small local consumer co-operatives.[9][10]

sentences.en: In the first 15 years, many co-operatives were established, thanks to the autarky of the market and the awakening of the Spanish economy.
sentences.zh: 在最初的15年里，由于市场的自给自足和西班牙经济的觉醒，许多合作社成立了。

sentences.en: During these years, also with the encouragement of Arizmendiarrieta, the Caja Laboral ("Labor savings bank", 1959) and the Social Welfare Body Lagun Aro ("Friend/help time", 1966) were established that played a key role.
sentences.zh: 在这些年里，同样在 Arizmendiarrieta 的鼓励下，Caja Laboral（“劳工储蓄银行”，1959 年）和社会福利机构 Lagun Aro（“朋友/帮助时间”，1966 年）的成立发挥了关键作用。

sentences.en: The first local group was created, Ularco.
sentences.zh: 第一个本地团体 Ularco 成立。

sentences.en: In 1969, Eroski was founded by merging ten small local consumer co-operatives.[9][10]
sentences.zh: 1969 年，Eroski 通过合并 10 个当地小型消费合作社成立。[9][10]

blocks.html_en: During the next 20 years, from 1970 to 1990, the dynamic continued, with a strong increase in new co-operatives promoted by Caja Laboral's Business Division, the promotion of co-operative associations, the formation of local groups, and the founding of the Ikerlan ("Research work") research centre in 1974.[11]

sentences.en: During the next 20 years, from 1970 to 1990, the dynamic continued, with a strong increase in new co-operatives promoted by Caja Laboral's Business Division, the promotion of co-operative associations, the formation of local groups, and the founding of the Ikerlan ("Research work") research centre in 1974.[11]
sentences.zh: 在接下来的 20 年中，从 1970 年到 1990 年，这种动态持续存在，Caja Laboral 业务部推动的新合作社的强劲增长、合作社协会的推广、地方团体的形成以及 1974 年 Ikerlan（“研究工作”）研究中心的成立。 [11]

blocks.html_en: With Spain scheduled to join the European Economic Community in 1986, it was decided in 1984 to establish the "Mondragon Co-operative Group", the forerunner of the current corporation. In-service training for managers was strengthened by creating Otalora, dedicated to training, and the dissemination of co-operatives. The Group consisted of 23,130 workers at the end of 1990.[12][non-primary source needed]

sentences.en: With Spain scheduled to join the European Economic Community in 1986, it was decided in 1984 to establish the "Mondragon Co-operative Group", the forerunner of the current corporation.
sentences.zh: 随着西班牙计划于1986年加入欧洲经济共同体，1984年决定成立“蒙德拉贡合作集团”，即现在公司的前身。

sentences.en: In-service training for managers was strengthened by creating Otalora, dedicated to training, and the dissemination of co-operatives.
sentences.zh: 通过创建 Otalora，致力于培训和合作社的传播，加强了管理人员的在职培训。

sentences.en: The Group consisted of 23,130 workers at the end of 1990.[12][non-primary source needed]
sentences.zh: 截至 1990 年底，该集团由 23,130 名工人组成。[12][需要非主要来源]

blocks.html_en: International expansion

sentences.en: International expansion
sentences.zh: 国际扩张

blocks.html_en: [edit]

On the international stage, the aim was to respond to growing globalisation, expanding abroad by establishing production plants in a number of countries. The first was the Copreci plant in Mexico in 1990, followed by many others: up to 73 by the end of 2008, and 122 at the end of 2013. The goals were to increase competitiveness and market share, bring component supply closer to customers' plants, especially in the automotive and domestic appliance sectors, and to strengthen employment in the Basque Country by promoting exports of co-operatives' products by means of new platforms.[13]

sentences.en: On the international stage, the aim was to respond to growing globalisation, expanding abroad by establishing production plants in a number of countries.
sentences.zh: 在国际舞台上，其目标是应对日益发展的全球化，通过在多个国家建立生产工厂来向海外扩张。

sentences.en: The first was the Copreci plant in Mexico in 1990, followed by many others: up to 73 by the end of 2008, and 122 at the end of 2013.
sentences.zh: 第一个是 1990 年位于墨西哥的 Copreci 工厂，随后是许多其他工厂：到 2008 年底达到 73 个，到 2013 年底达到 122 个。

sentences.en: The goals were to increase competitiveness and market share, bring component supply closer to customers' plants, especially in the automotive and domestic appliance sectors, and to strengthen employment in the Basque Country by promoting exports of co-operatives' products by means of new platforms.[13]
sentences.zh: 目标是提高竞争力和市场份额，使零部件供应更接近客户工厂，特别是在汽车和家用电器行业，并通过新平台促进合作社产品出口来加强巴斯克地区的就业。 [13]

blocks.html_en: Between 2002 and 2007, Fagor and Eroski issued bonds (aportaciones subordinadas). While they were commercialized as safe deposits, the courts classed them as riskier debt instruments. When the yields fell during the 2008 financial crisis, bond-holders sued against the cooperatives.[14]

sentences.en: Between 2002 and 2007, Fagor and Eroski issued bonds (aportaciones subordinadas).
sentences.zh: 2002 年至 2007 年间，Fagor 和 Eroski 发行了债券（次级捐款）。

sentences.en: While they were commercialized as safe deposits, the courts classed them as riskier debt instruments.
sentences.zh: 虽然它们作为安全存款进行商业化，但法院将它们归类为风险较高的债务工具。

sentences.en: When the yields fell during the 2008 financial crisis, bond-holders sued against the cooperatives.[14]
sentences.zh: 2008 年金融危机期间，当收益率下降时，债券持有人对合作社提起诉讼。 [14]

blocks.html_en: In 2008, the worker-owners of the cooperatives Ampo (metal casting) and Irizar (coaches) voted to leave the corporation.[14]

sentences.en: In 2008, the worker-owners of the cooperatives Ampo (metal casting) and Irizar (coaches) voted to leave the corporation.[14]
sentences.zh: 2008 年，Ampo（金属铸造）和 Irizar（教练）合作社的工人业主投票决定离开公司。 [14]

blocks.html_en: In October 2009, the United Steelworkers announced an agreement with Mondragon to create worker cooperatives in the United States.[15] On 26 March 2012, the USW, Mondragon, and the Ohio Employee Ownership Center (OEOC) announced their detailed union co-op model.[16]

sentences.en: In October 2009, the United Steelworkers announced an agreement with Mondragon to create worker cooperatives in the United States.[15] On 26 March 2012, the USW, Mondragon, and the Ohio Employee Ownership Center (OEOC) announced their detailed union co-op model.[16]
sentences.zh: 2009年10月，美国钢铁工人联合会宣布与蒙德拉贡达成协议，在美国创建工人合作社。 [15] 2012 年 3 月 26 日，USW、蒙德拉贡和俄亥俄州员工所有权中心 (OEOC) 宣布了他们详细的工会合作模式。 [16]

blocks.html_en: The industrial sector ended 2012 with a new record of €4 billion in international sales, beating sales figures from before the 2008 financial crisis. Mondragon opened 11 new production subsidiaries. International sales that year accounted for 69% of all sales, a 26% increase from 2009 to 2012, and with 14,000 employees abroad. Mondragon's share in the BRIC markets increased to 20% compared to the previous year.[17] In 2013, international sales grew by 6.7% and accounted for 71.1% of total sales.[18]

sentences.en: The industrial sector ended 2012 with a new record of €4 billion in international sales, beating sales figures from before the 2008 financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 2012 年工业部门的国际销售额创下了 40 亿欧元的新纪录，超过了 2008 年金融危机之前的销售额。

sentences.en: Mondragon opened 11 new production subsidiaries.
sentences.zh: 蒙德拉贡开设了 11 家新的生产子公司。

sentences.en: International sales that year accounted for 69% of all sales, a 26% increase from 2009 to 2012, and with 14,000 employees abroad.
sentences.zh: 当年国际销售额占全部销售额的69%，比2009年至2012年增长了26%，在海外拥有14,000名员工。

sentences.en: Mondragon's share in the BRIC markets increased to 20% compared to the previous year.[17] In 2013, international sales grew by 6.7% and accounted for 71.1% of total sales.[18]
sentences.zh: 蒙德拉贡在金砖四国市场的份额较上年增长至20%。[17] 2013年，国际销售额增长6.7%，占总销售额的71.1%。[18]

blocks.html_en: On 16 October 2013, domestic appliance company Fagor Electrodomésticos filed for bankruptcy under Spanish law to renegotiate €1.1 billion of debt, after suffering heavy losses during the euro area crisis and the 2008–2014 Spanish real estate crisis, putting 5,600 employees at risk of losing their jobs.[19] This was followed by the bankruptcy of the whole Fagor group on 6 November 2013.[20] In July 2014, Fagor was bought by Catalonian company Cata for €42.5 million. Cata pledged to create 705 direct jobs in the Basque Country and to continue the brand names Fagor, Edesa, Aspes, and Splendid.[21]

sentences.en: On 16 October 2013, domestic appliance company Fagor Electrodomésticos filed for bankruptcy under Spanish law to renegotiate €1.1 billion of debt, after suffering heavy losses during the euro area crisis and the 2008–2014 Spanish real estate crisis, putting 5,600 employees at risk of losing their jobs.[19] This was followed by the bankruptcy of the whole Fagor group on 6 November 2013.[20] In July 2014, Fagor was bought by Catalonian company Cata for €42.5 million.
sentences.zh: 2013 年 10 月 16 日，家用电器公司 Fagor Electrodomésticos 在欧元区危机和 2008-2014 年西班牙房地产危机中遭受重大损失，导致 5,600 名员工面临失业风险后，根据西班牙法律申请破产，以重新谈判 11 亿欧元的债务。 [19]随后整个法格集团于 2013 年 11 月 6 日破产。[20] 2014 年 7 月，发格被加泰罗尼亚公司 Cata 以 4250 万欧元收购。

sentences.en: Cata pledged to create 705 direct jobs in the Basque Country and to continue the brand names Fagor, Edesa, Aspes, and Splendid.[21]
sentences.zh: Cata 承诺在巴斯克地区创造 705 个直接就业机会，并继续使用 Fagor、Edesa、Aspes 和 Splendid 品牌。[21]

blocks.html_en: In 2022, the worker-owners of ULMA Group (scaffolding) and Orona (elevators) voted to leave the corporation. Estimated impact of the leave is a workforce drop by 13% and a 15% cut of the group's sales.[22] As successful cooperatives they were contributing 10% of their profit to a common fund supporting ailing cooperatives. They will not contribute to the solidarity fund but they will keep insuring their workers with Lagun Aro and collaborate with Mondragon Unibertsitatea and other cooperatives in the group.[14]

sentences.en: In 2022, the worker-owners of ULMA Group (scaffolding) and Orona (elevators) voted to leave the corporation.
sentences.zh: 2022 年，ULMA 集团（脚手架）和 Orona（电梯）的工人业主投票决定离开公司。

sentences.en: Estimated impact of the leave is a workforce drop by 13% and a 15% cut of the group's sales.[22] As successful cooperatives they were contributing 10% of their profit to a common fund supporting ailing cooperatives.
sentences.zh: 休假的估计影响是劳动力减少 13%，集团销售额减少 15%。 [22]作为成功的合作社，他们将利润的 10% 捐献给一个共同基金，以支持陷入困境的合作社。

sentences.en: They will not contribute to the solidarity fund but they will keep insuring their workers with Lagun Aro and collaborate with Mondragon Unibertsitatea and other cooperatives in the group.[14]
sentences.zh: 他们不会向团结基金捐款，但将继续为 Lagun Aro 的工人提供保险，并与 Mondragon Unibertsitatea 和该集团的其他合作社合作。 [14]

blocks.html_en: Mondragon co-operatives are united by a humanist concept of business, a philosophy of participation and solidarity, and a shared business culture. The culture is rooted in a shared mission and a number of principles, corporate values and business policies.[23]

sentences.en: Mondragon co-operatives are united by a humanist concept of business, a philosophy of participation and solidarity, and a shared business culture.
sentences.zh: 蒙德拉贡合作社以人文主义商业理念、参与和团结的理念以及共同的商业文化团结在一起。

sentences.en: The culture is rooted in a shared mission and a number of principles, corporate values and business policies.[23]
sentences.zh: 这种文化植根于共同的使命和一系列原则、企业价值观和商业政策。[23]

blocks.html_en: Over the years, these links have been embodied in a series of operating rules approved on a majority basis by the Co-operative Congresses, which regulate the activity of the Governing Bodies of the corporation (Standing Committee, General Council), the Grassroots Co-operatives and the Divisions they belong to, from the organisational, institutional and economic points of view as well as in terms of assets.[24][non-primary source needed]

sentences.en: Over the years, these links have been embodied in a series of operating rules approved on a majority basis by the Co-operative Congresses, which regulate the activity of the Governing Bodies of the corporation (Standing Committee, General Council), the Grassroots Co-operatives and the Divisions they belong to, from the organisational, institutional and economic points of view as well as in terms of assets.[24][non-primary source needed]
sentences.zh: 多年来，这些联系已体现在合作社大会以多数票通过的一系列运作规则中，这些规则从组织、制度和经济角度以及资产方面规范了公司领导机构（常务委员会、总理事会）、基层合作社及其所属部门的活动。[24][需要非主要来源]

sentences.zh: Iñigo Ucín 自 2016 年起担任 Mondragon Corporation 总裁

blocks.html_en: This framework of business culture has been structured based on a common culture derived from the 10 Basic Co-operative Principles, in which Mondragon is rooted: Open Admission, Democratic Organisation, the Sovereignty of Labour, Instrumental and Subordinate Nature of Capital, Participatory Management, Payment Solidarity, Inter-cooperation, Social Transformation, Universality and Education.[25][non-primary source needed]

sentences.en: This framework of business culture has been structured based on a common culture derived from the 10 Basic Co-operative Principles, in which Mondragon is rooted: Open Admission, Democratic Organisation, the Sovereignty of Labour, Instrumental and Subordinate Nature of Capital, Participatory Management, Payment Solidarity, Inter-cooperation, Social Transformation, Universality and Education.[25][non-primary source needed]
sentences.zh: 这一商业文化框架是基于源自蒙德拉贡的 10 项基本合作原则的共同文化而构建的，蒙德拉贡的根源在于：开放准入、民主组织、劳动主权、资本的工具性和从属性、参与性管理、支付团结、相互合作、社会转型、普遍性和教育。[25][需要非主要来源]

blocks.html_en: This philosophy is complemented by four corporate values: Co-operation, acting as owners and protagonists; Participation, which takes shape as a commitment to management; Social Responsibility, by means of the distribution of wealth based on solidarity; and Innovation, focusing on constant renewal in all areas.[26]

sentences.en: This philosophy is complemented by four corporate values: Co-operation, acting as owners and protagonists; Participation, which takes shape as a commitment to management; Social Responsibility, by means of the distribution of wealth based on solidarity; and Innovation, focusing on constant renewal in all areas.[26]
sentences.zh: 这一理念得到了四个企业价值观的补充：合作、充当所有者和主角；参与，形成对管理的承诺；社会责任，通过基于团结的财富分配；和创新，注重各个领域的不断更新。[26]

blocks.html_en: This business culture translates into compliance with a number of Basic Objectives (Customer Focus, Development, Innovation, Profitability, People in Co-operation and Involvement in the Community) and General Policies approved by the Co-operative Congress, which are taken on board at all the corporation's organisational levels and incorporated into the four-year strategic plans and the annual business plans of the individual co-operatives, divisions, and the corporation as a whole.[27][non-primary source needed]

blocks.html_en: At Mondragon, there are agreed-upon wage ratios between executive work and field or factory work which earns a minimum wage. These ratios range from 3:1 to 9:1 in different cooperatives and average 5:1. That is, the general manager of an average Mondragon cooperative earns no more than 5 times as much as the theoretical minimum wage paid in their cooperative. For most workers, this ratio is smaller because there are few Mondragon worker-owners that earn minimum wages, because most jobs are somewhat specialized and are classified at higher wage levels. Mondragon Corporation
Type工人合作社联合会
成立14 April 1956
创始人何塞·玛丽亚·阿里兹门迪亚列塔
总部西班牙巴斯克自治区蒙德拉贡
服务区域国际的
关键人物佩洛·罗德里格斯（总理事会主席）[
收入112.13 亿欧元（2024 年）[1]
员工人数70,085 (2024)[1]
部门金融、工业、零售、知识[1]
网站mondragon-corporation.com

蒙德拉贡公司是一家位于西班牙巴斯克地区的公司和工人合作社联合会。

它于 1956 年由 José María Arizmendiarrieta 神父和他创办的一所技术学院的一群学生在蒙德拉贡镇创立。 它的第一个产品是石蜡加热器。

按资产周转率计算，它是西班牙第七大公司，也是巴斯克地区领先的商业集团。 截至 2016 年底，该公司在 257 家公司和组织中雇用了 74,117 名员工，涉及四个活动领域：金融、工业、零售和知识。 [2]截至2019年，就业人数81,507人。[3] 2024 年，该公司拥有超过 70,000 名工人，其中 30,660 人在巴斯克地区，29,340 人在西班牙其他地区，约 10,000 人在国外。[4]蒙德拉贡合作社按照国际合作社联盟维护的合作社身份声明进行运营。

1941年，作为一名年轻的天主教神父，何塞·玛丽亚·阿里兹曼迪亚里亚塔 (José María Arizmendiarrieta) 定居在蒙德拉贡 (Mondragón)，这座人口只有 7,000 人的小镇尚未从西班牙内战的贫困、饥饿、流放和紧张局势中恢复过来。[5][6] 1943 年，Arizmendiarrieta 建立了一所技术学院，成为当地公司（主要是合作社）经理、工程师和熟练工人的培训基地。 [7]

Arizmendiarrieta 花了数年时间教育年轻人一种基于团结和参与的人文主义形式，与天主教社会教义相协调，以及在创建第一个合作社之前获得必要的技术知识的重要性。

1955年，他挑选了五位年轻人成立了蒙德拉贡公司第一家合作社和工业公司。 该公司名为 Talleres Ulgor（“Ulgor 作坊”），是源自 Usatorre、Larrañaga、Gorroñogoitia、Ormaechea 和 Ortubay 等姓氏的缩写，今天称为 Fagor Electrodomésticos（西班牙语，意为“法格电器”）。[8][需要页面]

在最初的15年里，由于市场的自给自足和西班牙经济的觉醒，许多合作社成立了。 在这些年里，同样在 Arizmendiarrieta 的鼓励下，Caja Laboral（“劳工储蓄银行”，1959 年）和社会福利机构 Lagun Aro（“朋友/帮助时间”，1966 年）的成立发挥了关键作用。 第一个本地团体 Ularco 成立。 1969 年，Eroski 通过合并 10 个当地小型消费合作社成立。[9][10]

在接下来的 20 年中，从 1970 年到 1990 年，这种动态持续存在，Caja Laboral 业务部推动的新合作社的强劲增长、合作社协会的推广、地方团体的形成以及 1974 年 Ikerlan（“研究工作”）研究中心的成立。 [11]

随着西班牙计划于1986年加入欧洲经济共同体，1984年决定成立“蒙德拉贡合作集团”，即现在公司的前身。 通过创建 Otalora，致力于培训和合作社的传播，加强了管理人员的在职培训。 截至 1990 年底，该集团由 23,130 名工人组成。[12][需要非主要来源]

国际扩张

[edit]

在国际舞台上，其目标是应对日益发展的全球化，通过在多个国家建立生产工厂来向海外扩张。 第一个是 1990 年位于墨西哥的 Copreci 工厂，随后是许多其他工厂：到 2008 年底达到 73 个，到 2013 年底达到 122 个。 目标是提高竞争力和市场份额，使零部件供应更接近客户工厂，特别是在汽车和家用电器行业，并通过新平台促进合作社产品出口来加强巴斯克地区的就业。 [13]

2002 年至 2007 年间，Fagor 和 Eroski 发行了债券（次级捐款）。 虽然它们作为安全存款进行商业化，但法院将它们归类为风险较高的债务工具。 2008 年金融危机期间，当收益率下降时，债券持有人对合作社提起诉讼。 [14]

2008 年，Ampo（金属铸造）和 Irizar（教练）合作社的工人业主投票决定离开公司。 [14]

2009年10月，美国钢铁工人联合会宣布与蒙德拉贡达成协议，在美国创建工人合作社。 [15] 2012 年 3 月 26 日，USW、蒙德拉贡和俄亥俄州员工所有权中心 (OEOC) 宣布了他们详细的工会合作模式。 [16]

2012 年工业部门的国际销售额创下了 40 亿欧元的新纪录，超过了 2008 年金融危机之前的销售额。 蒙德拉贡开设了 11 家新的生产子公司。 当年国际销售额占全部销售额的69%，比2009年至2012年增长了26%，在海外拥有14,000名员工。 蒙德拉贡在金砖四国市场的份额较上年增长至20%。[17] 2013年，国际销售额增长6.7%，占总销售额的71.1%。[18]

2013 年 10 月 16 日，家用电器公司 Fagor Electrodomésticos 在欧元区危机和 2008-2014 年西班牙房地产危机中遭受重大损失，导致 5,600 名员工面临失业风险后，根据西班牙法律申请破产，以重新谈判 11 亿欧元的债务。 [19]随后整个法格集团于 2013 年 11 月 6 日破产。[20] 2014 年 7 月，发格被加泰罗尼亚公司 Cata 以 4250 万欧元收购。 Cata 承诺在巴斯克地区创造 705 个直接就业机会，并继续使用 Fagor、Edesa、Aspes 和 Splendid 品牌。[21]

2022 年，ULMA 集团（脚手架）和 Orona（电梯）的工人业主投票决定离开公司。 休假的估计影响是劳动力减少 13%，集团销售额减少 15%。 [22]作为成功的合作社，他们将利润的 10% 捐献给一个共同基金，以支持陷入困境的合作社。 他们不会向团结基金捐款，但将继续为 Lagun Aro 的工人提供保险，并与 Mondragon Unibertsitatea 和该集团的其他合作社合作。 [14]

蒙德拉贡合作社以人文主义商业理念、参与和团结的理念以及共同的商业文化团结在一起。 这种文化植根于共同的使命和一系列原则、企业价值观和商业政策。[23]

多年来，这些联系已体现在合作社大会以多数票通过的一系列运作规则中，这些规则从组织、制度和经济角度以及资产方面规范了公司领导机构（常务委员会、总理事会）、基层合作社及其所属部门的活动。[24][需要非主要来源]

这一商业文化框架是基于源自蒙德拉贡的 10 项基本合作原则的共同文化而构建的，蒙德拉贡的根源在于：开放准入、民主组织、劳动主权、资本的工具性和从属性、参与性管理、支付团结、相互合作、社会转型、普遍性和教育。[25][需要非主要来源]

这一理念得到了四个企业价值观的补充：合作、充当所有者和主角；参与，形成对管理的承诺；社会责任，通过基于团结的财富分配；和创新，注重各个领域的不断更新。[26]

这种商业文化转化为遵守合作社代表大会批准的一系列基本目标（以客户为中心、发展、创新、盈利、人员合作和参与社区）和一般政策，这些目标在公司的所有组织层面上得到采纳，并纳入各个合作社、部门和整个公司的四年战略计划和年度业务计划中。[27][需要非主要来源]

在蒙德拉贡，行政工作与赚取最低工资的现场或工厂工作之间存在商定的工资比率。 不同合作社的比例从 3:1 到 9:1 不等，平均为 5:1。 也就是说，蒙德拉贡合作社总经理的平均收入不超过其合作社理论最低工资的5倍。 对于大多数工人来说，这个比例较小，因为很少有蒙德拉贡工人业主赚取最低工资，因为大多数工作都有些专业化，并且属于较高的工资水平。 合作社的工资比例由其工人业主通过民主投票定期决定。 [28]

与当地行业的类似工作相比，蒙德拉贡经理的工资在 1991 年低了 30%（因为一些公司支付给最高薪经理的工资是公司最低薪员工的数百倍）[29]，而中层管理人员、技术和专业级别的工资则低了 30%。 较低的工资水平比当地企业的类似工作平均高出 13%。 西班牙的累进税率进一步缩小了薪酬差距。[28]这些相对较低的工资使得从投资者拥有的公司招聘经理变得非常困难。 [30]

蒙德拉贡公司业务涉及四个领域：金融、工业、零售和知识，后者使蒙德拉贡有别于其他商业集团。 2013 年，该公司总收入超过 120 亿欧元（约合 160 亿美元），雇用了 74,061 名员工，[2] 使其成为西班牙第四大工业集团和第十大金融集团。[31]

该领域包括 Laboral Kutxa（Caja Laboral 的继任者）的银行业务、保险公司 Seguros Lagun Aro 以及自愿社会福利机构 Lagun Aro，截至 2014 年底，该机构的资产基金总额为 55.66 亿欧元。 该基金的收益用于支付长期退休金、丧偶福利和伤残福利，以补充西班牙社会保障体系提供的福利。

该公司旗下公司生产消费品、资本货物、工业零部件、产品以及建筑和服务系统。 后者包括非常多样化的业务群体，例如：

  • Abantail：自适应设计优化
  • Alecop：工程培训
  • LKS Consultores：法律服务
  • KREAN：建筑师和工程师。
  • MCCTelecom：电信工程。
  • Mondragon Lingua：​​翻译和语言学校
  • Mondragon Sistemas：自动化、工业计算和电信。
  • Ondoan：能源和环境领域的交钥匙项目。 在休闲和运动领域，它生产 Orbea 自行车、健身器材以及露营、花园和海滩用品。[32]

[33]

在资本货物方面，Mondragon 2009 年营业额为 9.76 亿欧元，是西班牙领先的机械加工（Danobat 集团）和钣金成型（Fagor Arrasate 集团）机床制造商。 这些机器还辅以机床、包装机械、自动化装配过程和木材加工机械、叉车、电力变压器、餐饮业集成设备、冷库和制冷设备的自动化和控制产品。 该公司专门专注于汽车行业，还生产各种铸铁和铸铝模具和工装，并在铸造行业的机械领域占据领先地位。 [34]

在工业零部件领域，蒙德拉贡 2009 年的营业额为 15 亿欧元，在该领域，蒙德拉贡作为领先汽车制造商的综合供应商，提供从零件的设计和开发到工业化以及零部件和组件的供应。 它拥有不同的业务部门，如制动器、车轴、悬架、变速器、发动机、铝轮圈、流体传导以及其他车辆内外部件。 它还为国内主要家电制造商生产白色家电、家居舒适和电子产品三个业务领域的零部件。 它生产用于石油天然气、石化厂和发电处理的法兰和管道配件、铜和铝电导体以及输送机部件。[35]

建筑业 2009 年销售额总计 9.74 亿欧元。 蒙德拉贡建造了建筑物和重要的基础设施项目。 它设计和建造大型金属（URSSA）、层压木和预制混凝土结构；供应聚合物混凝土预制件；提供模板和结构（ULMA 集团）以及公共工程机械和施工过程工业化的解决方案[流行语]，包括工程和装配服务。 ORONA 集团生产电梯。[36]

在商业服务方面，2008 年销售额总计 2.48 亿欧元，包括商业咨询服务、建筑和工程、房地产咨询、设计和创新（LKS 集团）、机电安装系统工程以及综合物流工程。 它还提供现代语言服务、制造教育设备并提供图形艺术服务 (mccgraphics S.Coop)。[需要引用]

2013年，71.1%的营业额来自国际销售。 产品出口到国外的销售额以及位于不同国家的 122 家子公司的生产产生的销售额：中国 (15)、法国 (17)、波兰 (8)、捷克共和国 (7)、墨西哥 (8)、巴西 (5)、德国 (4)、意大利 (4)、英国 (3)、罗马尼亚 (3)、美国 (4)、土耳其 (2)、葡萄牙 (2)、斯洛伐克 (2)、印度 (5)、泰国 (1) 和摩洛哥 (1)。 总体而言，2013 年这 122 家工厂为超过 11,000 人提供了工作。 靠近上海的昆山企业工业园拥有七家子公司。[37] 2012年，该公司在海外开设了11家新子公司，雇用了约14,000名员工。 当年其国际销售额占总销售额的 69%（58 亿欧元，较上年下降 2%）创下历史新高。 蒙德拉贡还参与了91个国际研发项目。[38]

2014年，产业合作社创造了1000个就业岗位，国际化进程继续推进，在国外设立了125家生产子公司，比上年增加了3家。[39]

Mondragon 经营着 Eroski，这是西班牙和法国南部领先的零售集团之一，并与法国集团 Les Mousquetaires 和德国零售商 Edeka 保持密切联系，并于 2002 年与后者成立了 Alidis 国际采购集团。 工人所有者和消费者成员参与合作社的决策机构和 Eroski 的管理。 [40]截至 2013 年底，Eroski 营业额达 66 亿欧元，经营 2.069 家商店，其中包括 90 家 Eroski 大卖场、1,211 家 Eroski/center、Caprabo、Eroski/city、Aliprox、Familia、Onda 和现购自运超市、155 家 Eroski 旅行社分店、63 个加油站、39 家 Forum Sport 商店和 221 家 IF 香水商店。[41] Eroski 在法国南部拥有 4 家大型超市、16 家超市和 17 家加油站，在安道尔拥有 4 家香水店。 [42]

零售业包括食品集团 Erkop，从事餐饮、清洁、畜牧业和园艺业务；Auzo Lagun 是一家提供集体餐饮、建筑物和场所清洁以及卫生部门综合服务的合作社。 [43] 2008年，工人会员投票决定将合作社转型扩大到整个零售集团，将子公司转变为合作社，并使受薪工人成为工人会员。 [44]

该领域具有双重重点：教育培训和创新，这两者都是公司发展的关键要素。 Polyteknika Ikastegia Txorierri、Arizmendi Icastola 和 Lea Artibai Ikastetxea 是世界上最重要的大学。

蒙德拉贡大学是一所合作型大学，将知识、技能和价值观的发展结合起来，并与企业界尤其是蒙德拉贡合作社保持着密切的关系。 技术创新是通过合作社自己的研发部门、企业科技计划、公司的 12 个技术中心和 Garaia 创新园产生的。[47]

15个技术中心在重点领域的发展中发挥着基础性作用。 2009 年，他们雇用了 742 名员工，预算为 5,370 万欧元。[48] 2013 年，其技术中心和研发单位网络为 1,700 人提供了就业机会，对研发和创新事务的投入达 1.36 亿欧元，占附加值的 8.5%。 [18]蒙德拉贡拥有479族发明专利，占巴斯克地区专利的25%，参与了30多个欧洲层面的研发合作项目。 [39]

2012 年，理查德·D. 美国经济学教授沃尔夫盛赞蒙德拉贡的一系列企业，包括为员工提供良好的工资、赋予普通工人决策权以及女性工人的平等措施，认为这是一项重大成功，并称其为替代资本主义生产方式的工作模式。 [49]

在 2012 年 4 月的一次采访中，诺姆·乔姆斯基 (Noam Chomsky) 表示，虽然蒙德拉贡提供了资本主义的替代方案，但它仍然根植于限制蒙德拉贡决策的资本主义体系中：[50]

以最先进的案例为例：蒙德拉贡。 它是工人拥有的，不是工人管理的，虽然管理层确实经常来自劳动力，但这是在市场体系中，他们仍然剥削南美的工人，他们做对整个社会有害的事情，他们别无选择。 如果你处于一个必须盈利才能生存的系统中，你就不得不忽视负外部性以及对他人的影响。

维森斯·纳瓦罗写道，从商业角度来看，蒙德拉贡成功地将效率与团结和民主相结合。 然而，他写道，非业主雇员的数量比工人业主的增长速度更快，以至于在一些公司中，例如在蒙德拉贡拥有的连锁超市中，前者的群体比后者大得多。 在纳瓦罗看来，这建立了一个两级系统——例如，在公司倒闭的情况下拯救谁。 在发格的倒闭中，员工被转移到蒙德拉贡旗下的其他公司，这对那些工人所有者有利，这可能会影响劳资关系：[51]

事实上，蒙德拉贡的成功之一是它能够在公司内部的工人中创造一种认同感，鼓励他们之间团结和合作的环境，这种感觉也延伸到了非工人业主（尽管程度要小得多）。 然而，后者感受到的联系有所减弱，暴露了合作社的一个弱点。

蒙德拉贡系统是《资本与债务陷阱》中分析的四个案例研究之一，该研究总结了证据，表明合作社往往比传统管理的组织更能持续更长的时间，并且更不易受到不当激励和其他组织治理问题的影响。

杰克逊合作社是美国密西西比州杰克逊市的一个工人合作社网络，其创始人将蒙德拉贡视为主要灵感来源。 [52]
